Formulation  
Patient presents with a gradually worsening headache over three days, characterized as dull with occasional sharp pain, predominantly around the right eye. Family history of migraines is a significant predisposing factor. The headache impacts concentration and work performance, possibly exacerbated by workplace screen exposure and recent project-related stress. Treatment with ibuprofen has been ineffective at the current dose. No red flag symptoms (e.g., vision loss, neurological deficits) noted. Protective factors include patient’s insight and willingness to engage in management. Referral for stronger analgesia and headache diary recommended to identify triggers. Follow-up planned to assess response and consider prophylactic treatment if needed.

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Suspected migraine headache  
- Patient Goal(s):  
  - Achieve effective pain relief and reduce headache frequency and severity  
  - Improve ability to concentrate and perform work duties  
- Clinical Goal(s):  
  - Provide adequate analgesic management to relieve current headache  
  - Identify triggers and monitor headache pattern using a headache diary  
  - Assess need for prophylactic therapy during follow-up  
- Actions (Patient):  
  - Take prescribed medication as directed (consider Naproxen, Paracetamol, or Codeine)  
  - Keep a headache diary to document frequency, intensity, and possible triggers  
  - Return for review in 1-2 weeks or earlier if symptoms worsen  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  - Prescribe appropriate stronger analgesics (Naproxen, Paracetamol, Codeine)  
  - Educate patient on correct dosing of ibuprofen if continued use  
  - Recommend headache diary use for monitoring  
  - Arrange follow-up appointment in 1-2 weeks  
  - Provide guidance for urgent review if worsening symptoms or new neurological signs develop  

Secondary Problem: Possible stress-related headache exacerbation  
- Patient Goal(s):  
  - Manage work-related stress to minimize headache triggers  
- Clinical Goal(s):  
  - Identify and address workplace stressors contributing to symptoms  
- Actions (Patient):  
  - Modify work environment as able (e.g., reduce screen brightness)  
  - Practice stress management techniques as advised  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  - Discuss stress management strategies and possible referral if required  
  - Monitor impact of stress on headache during follow-up  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes  
  - Topics Covered: Headache types and triggers, medication use and dosing, importance of headache diary, when to seek urgent care  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing headache frequency or intensity, visual changes, weakness, speech difficulties, inability to function  
- Coping Strategies: Environmental modification (screen brightness), medication adherence, headache diary, stress management
